asked.text: Thanks for making the time. To start, tell me a bit about yourself and what brought you to this role.

answers.text: Sure. So um I'm an AI engineer. I built Verse, a meeting assistant for the Mac, and before that Trailhead, which is on the App Store. I like, you know, building things end to end.

coach: Clear start. Name the one project you want them to ask about.

asked.text: Describe a time you took an LLM feature from prototype to production.

answers.text: At Lantern we had invoices that people typed in by hand. I added an extraction step with a review screen. Basically the entry time dropped a lot and the team was happy, kind of a big win.
We looked at the time per document and at how often reviewers changed the output. Actually it was around 40 percent fewer corrections after the second prompt.

coach: Give the number: how long did entry take before and after?

asked.text: How would you keep latency and cost under control in a streaming LLM feature?

answers.text: In Verse I stream the first sentence as soon as it is complete and I cache the long prefix so repeat calls are cheap. Um, I also pick a small model for the fast path and a larger one for the deep answer.

coach: Good concrete mechanism. Add a measured latency figure.

candidate_question.text: What does the first quarter look like?
candidate_question.reply: You would start on the evaluation harness for the messaging assistant.
